about: Every board and committee the town posts for, one page each: what is coming, what happened, every vote we have minutes for, where the board’s time goes, and when budget season has fallen on its agendas in past years.

about_itself.label: School Committee Operating Protocols
about_itself.text:
Lunenburg School Committee Operating Protocols 
Who We Represent 
1. School Committee members are elected public officials, selected by their fellow citizens to act in their
interests and empowered to act as they see their duty to work for the children of their community.
Pertinent Points of School Committee Authority 
1. We shall exercise leadership in vision, planning, policy, budgeting, evaluation of the 
Superintendent of Schools, and advocacy of the district, consistent with the law and our 
policies.
2. It is the Superintendent’s responsibility to oversee personnel issues and to manage the day-
to-day operations of the district. It is the School Committee’s responsibility to evaluate the 
superintendent’s effectiveness in these matters in accordance with Department of Elementary 
and Secondary Education’s standards.
3. We shall recognize that authority rests only with the majority decision of the School 
Committee and we shall not make any independent commitments or take any independent 
actions that may compromise the School Committee as a whole. The Superintendent takes 
direction from the School Committee as a whole, not an individual member.
4. We shall follow the chain of command regarding questions, concerns or complaints and 
direct members of the community to do the same.
5. We shall not use our positions for personal or partisan gain.
6. When serious issues arise, the Superintendent, not any School Committee member, has the 
authority to investigate a complaint or concern. The Superintendent shall provide committee 
members with his/her response/resolution within an appropriate timeline.
How We Treat Each Other 
1. We shall debate the issues keeping an open mind to other member’s opinions and/or 
positions.
2. We shall respect staff and fellow committee members at all times.
3. We shall work to build trust between and among School Committee members, the 
Superintendent, the administration, faculty, staff and the community by treating everyone 
with dignity and respect, even in times of disagreement.
How We Communicate 
1. The Superintendent and the School Committee recognize the importance of proactive
communication. If School Committee members have questions or concerns, we agree to contact
the Superintendent well in advance of a meeting. We agree that there will be no surprises.

Lunenburg School Committee Operating Protocols 
 
2. We shall channel requests for information through the Superintendent and/or the School 
Committee Chairperson rather than directly to district staff.  
3. We shall provide full disclosure of information and not withhold information from other 
members.  
4. The Committee shall advocate for the public schools and public education as ambassadors of 
the school system by promoting support for public education and spreading the news of our 
success. We shall always strive to project a positive professional image.  
5. The Committee recognizes the Chairperson, or her/his designee, as the official voice of the 
School Committee.  
6. The Superintendent and the School Committee recognize the importance of working 
collaboratively with Town officials to improve our schools and we shall actively seek ways to 
enlist their support for our efforts. Town officials shall channel requests for information 
through the Chairperson for consideration by the School Committee 
7. Our seating plan allows all members to see and hear each other to facilitate effective 
communication. The School Committee members, Superintendent, and Student Representative 
will be seated at the table.  
 
How We Operate 
1. We acknowledge that a School Committee meeting is a meeting of the School Committee that 
is held in public – not a public meeting. Our meetings will be recorded whenever possible and 
we encourage public comment.  Agendas and supporting documents for meetings will be posted 
on the district website in advance of the meeting. 
2. We shall conduct business through a set agenda. Emerging items shall be addressed in 
subsequent meetings through planned agenda items unless it is determined by the School 
Committee Chairperson that it would be detrimental to delay the issue until a subsequent 
meeting. Requests to add items to an agenda shall be made to the Superintendent or the School 
Committee Chairperson.   All items for a School Committee agenda must be in accordance with 
the law.  
3. The agenda will include public comment promptly at the beginning of the meeting to allow 
the public to address agenda items and matters under the governance of the School Committee. 
A second public comment will be included at the end of the meeting, before Topics for Future 
Discussion, to allow the public to comment on items relative to this meeting, items not on the 
agenda, or items for future discussion. Comments must be limited to matters that fall under the 
governance of the School Committee.  
4. Public comment periods will be limited to 10 minutes and can only be extended by a majority 
vote of the Committee.  Individual speakers will be limited to 3 minutes.  Written public 
comments may be submitted to the Chair. 
5. Our meetings will be guided by Roberts Rules of Order.  
6. We shall strive to make each meeting effective and efficient giving each member an equal 
opportunity to express their views and opinions and to relay their input in a concise and topic-
Lunenburg School Committee Operating Protocols 
 
focused manner. No one member should monopolize the discussion. All remarks must be 
directed through the Chair. Remarks must be courteous in language and delivery.  
7. We shall make decisions based on information and not on personalities after considering 
data, the Superintendent’s recommendations, proposals, and suggestions. We will vote our 
convictions, avoid bias, and uphold the decision of the majority of the Committee once a 
decision is made.  
8. We shall exhibit professional conduct and behavior.  
9. We shall attend meetings well-prepared to discuss issues on the agenda and to participate in 
efficient decision-making.  
 
10. When we are in committee we will remain in our committee member role throughout the 
meeting.  
11. We shall ensure that we do not breach the open meeting laws by deliberating in any format 
outside of duly convened meetings of the committee.  
12. We shall respect the confidentiality of Executive Sessions.  
13. Our actions shall be consistent with the core values of the district, and be consistent with 
our vision.  
14. We recognize the importance of honoring our agreed upon operating protocols and we agree 
to take responsibility for reminding one another when we get off track.  
 
How We Will Improve  
1. All new School Committee members will attend an MASC orientation session as soon as 
practicable, but within one year of being elected.  
2. All members will be open to continued personal growth through participating in workshops 
or training opportunities.  
3. We shall review and revise operating protocols annually through a workshop.  
4. We shall set goals annually and discuss progress.

meetings.hook: Closed session on a complaint, the finance and operations director interview, and the paraprofessional pay schedule

items.agenda_line: 14.   Executive Session-pursuant to Massachusetts General
items.why_it_matters: The committee may close the session under Chapter 30A Section 21(a)(1) to discuss a complaint brought against a public officer, employee, staff member or individual (listed as an OML complaint, T. Loughlin); the public cannot attend that part.

items.agenda_line: a. In Person Interview Richard Mathieu, Director of Finance and Operations(3 min)
items.why_it_matters: The committee is listed to interview a candidate for the district's Director of Finance and Operations, a senior finance and operations post.

items.agenda_line: a. Revised Paraprofessional Salary Schedule (3 min)
items.why_it_matters: A revised pay schedule for paraprofessionals is listed as an action item, which affects what the district pays those staff.

items.agenda_line: h. Vote an Amount to Fund the Special Education Reserve Fund Approved at November 2026 Town Meeting (3 min)
items.why_it_matters: The committee is listed to vote an amount toward the Special Education Reserve Fund, which is tied to a Town Meeting approval.
The committee reviews and approves the payment warrants for this period, which are the district's bills paid.

items.agenda_line: b. Removal of Surplus Material (3 min)
items.why_it_matters: The committee is listed to act on removing surplus district material.

items.agenda_line: c. Beginning of Year Data Presentation (3 min)
items.why_it_matters: A presentation of beginning-of-year data about the schools is listed, with the Director of Teaching & Learning named as a guest.

items.agenda_line: d. COTA Position Change to .5 OT (3 min)
items.why_it_matters: A change to a COTA position, to a .5 OT position, is listed as an action item and touches school staffing.

items.agenda_line: e. Brooks House Redevelopment Proposal (3 min)
items.why_it_matters: A redevelopment proposal for the Brooks House is on the agenda, with the town Planning Director listed as a guest.

items.agenda_line: f. Amendment of School Calendar-Parent/Teacher Conferences (3 min)
items.why_it_matters: The committee is listed to amend the school calendar for parent/teacher conferences, which affects families' schedules.

items.agenda_line: g. Fall Athletics Report (3 min)
items.why_it_matters: A report on fall athletics, a service used by students and families, is listed.

items.agenda_line: j. Discussion of Track & Field (Turf) Future Costs
items.why_it_matters: The committee is listed to discuss future costs of the track and field turf, a school facility.

watch_next: Next School Committee meeting, Wednesday, October 7, expected to run longer.
The temporary director's contract, which the superintendent is to prepare.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted unanimously, by roll call, to retitle the business administrator job as director of finance and operations.
The new title adds facilities, technology, transportation, athletics and food service duties to the role.
The committee voted unanimously to approve a temporary director of finance and operations, available three days a week, to close out FY26 and build FY27.
The superintendent is to prepare the temporary director's contract; if a permanent director is hired, the temporary director would overlap for cleanup and the FY28 budget build.
The superintendent reported the athletic director resigned on 30 days' notice, and a half-time athletic director position has been posted.

why_it_matters: The person who prepares and presents the school budget is changing, with an interim in place for the FY26 close-out and FY27 work and a permanent hire not yet made, so the FY28 budget build may be done by someone new.

The broader title puts facilities, technology, transportation, athletics and food service under one finance-and-operations role, and the minutes say the duties were widened to match a higher salary, which touches the administration side of the school budget.

ours.headline: School Committee unanimously approved a new director of finance and operations title and hired a temporary director.

watch_next: November town meeting warrant: votes on the special education stabilization fund and the turf field/track feasibility study articles
A future School Committee vote on reratifying the corrected paraprofessional contract

what_happened.line: The committee again passed over ratifying the paraprofessional contract after salary-scale calculation errors were found.
Members voted unanimously to send a placeholder warrant article for a special education stabilization fund toward November town meeting.
A placeholder warrant article seeking money for a feasibility and schematic study of the turf field, track, drainage and retaining wall passed 5-0.
The committee passed over the business administrator position after its top candidate withdrew, and the job was reposted with a revised description and a higher salary range.
Members approved the eighth-grade Washington DC trip, switching student travel from a prior mode to train.

why_it_matters: A further delay in ratifying the paraprofessional contract means paraprofessionals' pay under the new agreement remains unsettled.
The two placeholder warrant articles put a special education stabilization fund and a turf field/track study before voters at the November town meeting.
The unfilled business administrator post, alongside a financial practices review with UMass Boston, touches who oversees the school budget while that review is underway.

ours.headline: Paraprofessional contract vote delayed again over salary-calculation errors; two placeholder warrant articles advanced

watch_next: School committee vote on the business administrator hire, expected next Wednesday
Town finance committee meeting the next night, where audit funding is on the agenda

what_happened.line: The school committee will vote next week on hiring a school business administrator, after publicly interviewing a candidate tonight.
The school department will ask the town finance committee to fund a financial and process audit of the school business office from the town's reserve rather than the school budget.
The committee ratified a new three-year contract for cafeteria workers.
Votes on committee operating protocols and this year's goals, including the Turkey Hill Elementary MSBA process, were pushed to next week.
The chair said override funding approved at the recent special town meeting is already being used to reduce second-grade class sizes.

why_it_matters: The business administrator runs school finance day to day, and the committee itself controls this hire and expects to decide it next week.
The proposed audit's funding source determines whose budget absorbs the cost, and it goes to the town finance committee for a decision, not the school committee.
The Turkey Hill Elementary MSBA process is an early procedural step that can lead toward a future building project and a town vote.

ours.headline: The school committee will hire its own next business administrator, deciding by vote next week after tonight's public interview.

watch_next: Special town meeting vote on warrant article 3 (citizens' petition, middle school sports/transportation) and an amount as heard additional state aid appropriation
Warrant article 2, expected to be passed over by its sponsor at town meeting

what_happened.line: Committee voted to restore a second-grade teacher and fund literacy support plus athletic transportation, rather than an outside audit or a second BCBA.
Committee voted to commit any citizens'-petition warrant article 3 funds, if appropriated at special town meeting, to restoring middle school sports.
Committee decided to hold Ignite tutoring at 36 grant-funded seats rather than expand, freeing money for the other scenarios.
Committee will refund transportation donations already collected from boosters and return that decision to the booster clubs.
The private-transportation waiver form will be dropped from final forms if the funding article passes at town meeting.

why_it_matters: The vote decides whether second-grade class sizes shrink and middle/high school literacy support expands, funded from additional state aid the town has not yet appropriated at special town meeting.
Whether middle school sports return depends on a citizens' petition warrant article at that same town meeting, not on this vote alone.
Families who paid privately for athletic transportation, or donated to boosters for it, may see refunds and a change to the waiver paperwork if the article passes.

ours.headline: The committee voted to restore a second-grade teacher and literacy funding over an audit or a second BCBA.

watch_next: The September 3rd special town meeting vote on the school committee's warrant article
The tabled FY26 budget update item, expected at a future meeting

what_happened.line: The committee voted to submit its own warrant article asking the September 3rd special town meeting for the full additional state education aid, rather than relying on a separate citizen petition.
The committee chose to amend and adopt the original petition language as its own article so only one request goes to town meeting.
The committee voted unanimously to ratify a new custodians union (AFSCME Council 93) contract.
The committee accepted several FY26 line item transfers covering overages in maintenance, custodial, transportation, guidance and high school administration salaries.
A further FY26 budget update was tabled rather than voted on.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked at the September 3rd special town meeting to decide how much of the additional FY27 state aid goes to the schools versus other town needs.
The new custodians' union contract sets pay and terms for school custodial staff and factors into future budgets.
The tabled FY26 budget update means the year's final school spending picture is not yet settled.

ours.headline: The school committee voted to submit its own warrant article demanding the full extra state aid for the September 3rd special town meeting.

watch_next: July 29th meeting: custodial union MOU return
November special town meeting: warrant article for additional FY27 school funding

what_happened.line: The committee approved a spending plan funding reading specialists, an expanded assistant principal role, tutoring seats, and a music teacher increase.
The committee voted on a warrant article for an additional sum for the FY27 school budget, to go to the Select Board and a November special town meeting; the roll call outcome was not fully audible.
The warrant article vote was tabled once, then taken back up after extended, heated debate over pushing for an earlier special town meeting instead of the town manager's proposed November timeline.
A custodial union memorandum of understanding was not voted because the union had not yet reviewed it; it is expected back around July 29th.

why_it_matters: If the warrant article advances, residents at a November special town meeting will be asked to add funding to the already-voted FY27 school budget, drawn from new state education receipts rather than local taxes.

The spending plan touches reading support at two elementary schools, a high school administrative position, online tutoring capacity, and music staffing -- some already committed from health-insurance savings regardless of the warrant article's outcome.
Whether the special town meeting happens in November or sooner determines how quickly any new positions or services could actually start.

ours.headline: The committee approved a spending plan and voted to send a warrant article to the Select Board for extra FY27 school funding.

watch_next: The July 29 school committee meeting, where football booster funding requests and fundraising policy return as agenda items.
Whether the select board schedules the requested special town meeting on state aid.

what_happened.line: The committee voted unanimously to ask the select board for a special town meeting to redirect state aid to schools.
A curriculum report accepted by the committee described zero reading interventionists left at two elementary schools.
Grades 3 and 4 will drop departmentalized teaching next year, moving to one teacher per class instead of rotating teams.
The personnel report, accepted with one abstention, listed numerous staff departures attributed to budget uncertainty.
Four routine line-item transfers passed unanimously, including shifting unspent athletic transportation funds to cover an athletic fees overage.

why_it_matters: A special town meeting request means residents may be asked to vote again on directing state aid into the school budget.

ours.headline: The committee voted unanimously to ask the select board for a special town meeting to redirect state aid into the school budget.

watch_next: Next School Committee meeting: discussion of district finances and whether to pursue another override or funding request
A public budget check before June 30, and action on the deferred line-item transfers

what_happened.line: After the override's defeat, the committee agreed to take up another override or funding request at its next meeting.
Line-item transfers were deferred to the following meeting, with a public budget check planned before June 30.
A proposed physical education credit or waiver for varsity athletes was tabled after two members were absent; the committee will gather information from peer districts first.
The committee voted unanimously to accept a Turkey Hill PTO donation and, later, the facilities and grounds report citing maintenance-contract savings.

The committee also took up FY27 school handbooks and authorizing the superintendent to negotiate a fifth-grade band stipend with the union, but the recording does not make the vote outcome on either audible.

why_it_matters: Another override vote or funding request may come back to residents, following the defeat of the prior one.
The deferred line-item transfers and the pre-June-30 budget check affect how the current fiscal year's school budget closes out.
The tabled PE credit/waiver would change graduation or scheduling requirements for varsity athletes if it comes back for a vote.

ours.headline: After the override's defeat, the committee agreed to weigh another override or funding request at its next meeting.

watch_next: The superintendent's report back on fifth-grade bus-release community feedback
Any future override vote or the community task force's recommendations

what_happened.line: After the override failed, the committee leaned toward implementing a balanced budget built on cuts to class sizes, interventionists, middle school sports and transportation, and high school world language, rather than returning to voters right away.
The committee elected Laura as chair and Tony as vice chair for 2026-2027, with Mandy Gilman named secretary pending her acceptance.
The fifth-grade bus-release procedure was tabled so the superintendent can gather community feedback before any change.
The committee adopted revised policies on cash handling, student data privacy, medication administration, and advertising in schools.
The committee accepted a composite evaluation of the superintendent's first year.

why_it_matters: The override's failure is now translating into specific reductions -- class sizes, interventionist staffing, middle school sports and transportation, and a high school language program -- while the committee weighs a community task force before deciding whether to ask voters again.
The new cash-handling policy sets a cap on cash accepted per school transaction, which came up directly in connection with how prom tickets can be sold going forward.

Families with fourth- and fifth-graders should watch for the superintendent's community feedback process on bus release, since it is being handled as an administrative procedure rather than a committee policy vote.

ours.headline: Override failed; committee accepts a balanced-budget of cuts and eyes another override attempt next year

watch_next: Written decision on the student-council election appeal, expected early the following week
Future meeting inviting parents to discuss the fifth-grade bus-release consent procedure

what_happened.line: Committee heard roughly 90 minutes of testimony on an appeal over a disputed student-council election and took no vote, reserving a written decision.
Members approved a batch of year-end line-item transfers, including moves among substitute-teacher lines and a special education paraprofessional account.
Committee voted to authorize applying for a federal literacy grant, capped at an amount as heard, and for FY27 DESE entitlement grants.
Discussion of loosening the fifth-grade school-bus release consent rule was deferred until the superintendent returns and new legal counsel weighs in.
Committee waived second reading on four policies covering cash handling, student data privacy, medication administration, and school advertising.

why_it_matters: The written decision on the election appeal will set how the district resolves nomination-signature disputes in student government going forward.
Year-end transfers show which school programs, including substitute teaching and special education paraprofessional support, ran short of their budgeted lines.
Any change to fifth-grade bus-release rules affects how parents authorize after-school pickup, and now waits on new legal review before moving forward.

ours.headline: Committee heard a 90-minute appeal over a disputed student-council election signature count, took no vote

watch_next: Superintendent evaluation rubric scores due around May 13, with compilation and discussion at the May 20 meeting
A future agenda item on an extended day program fee increase

what_happened.line: The superintendent and chair urged residents to approach the coming override vote and town meeting collaboratively, calling this year's budget process unusually transparent.
The committee voted to submit two Prism grant applications and a Farm to Table grant to bring in state funding for staff training and curriculum.
A dispute over a scholarship trust fund's EIN with the town's Trust Commission was sent to legal counsel rather than resolved tonight.
First readings were waived on four policies, including student data privacy and security rules that address AI use.
Negotiating teams were assigned for the custodians' and cafeteria workers' union contracts, and a fee increase for the extended day program was pushed to a future agenda.

why_it_matters: The override and town meeting the superintendent referenced would set the tax bill residents vote on, and the meeting framed this year's budget process as more transparent than past years.

ours.headline: Schools urged town unity ahead of the override vote; routine grants and policy readings were approved

watch_next: Business manager's revolving-fund and quarterly budget report, expected at the next meeting (April 15)
Contract negotiations, set to begin the following week with experienced and new members paired up

what_happened.line: The committee voted to continue charging the student bus fee for another year, despite members calling it unfair, citing the district's financial situation.
Members voted to end the district-run Lunenburg lifelong learning program effective June 1, citing minimal revenue and reliance on volunteers or a pass-through vendor.
The committee authorized the superintendent to pursue a one-time federal earmark to build a district-wide instructional framework and offset an expected cut to Title One funding.
Members endorsed a letter to state legislators arguing Lunenburg's Chapter 70 funding formula undercounts its per-pupil spending and excludes transportation costs.
The FY26 monthly budget report showed spending running ahead of the same point last year, with the electrical and legal lines over budget.

why_it_matters: The bus fee stays in place for families who use it, separate from and regardless of the outcome of the townwide override vote in May.
Ending the lifelong learning program removes a district-run adult offering, though students already enrolled will finish the current session before it closes.
The letter to legislators is an ask, not a change in funding -- any shift in how Chapter 70 treats transportation or per-pupil spending depends on action in Boston, not this committee.

ours.headline: Committee voted to keep charging the student bus fee despite members calling it unfair, citing budget desperation.

watch_next: May town meeting and ballot vote on the two-tier FY27 override
The stormwater task force's meeting the following day on a possible separate stormwater article

what_happened.line: The Select Board, Finance Committee and School Committee voted unanimously to pursue a two-tier FY27 override rather than a single override number.
The boards pulled stormwater out of the tier-two override and chose not to bring a standalone stormwater override article this cycle, deferring to the stormwater task force.
The School Committee raised its lower-tier override ask to restore fifth-grade band, leaving the higher tier unchanged.
Officials said they could not guarantee the higher override tier would avoid another override request next year, citing volatile costs like health insurance.
The boards agreed to bring in a paid communications professional to help plan joint messaging for town meeting and the ballot.

why_it_matters: A two-tier override means voters may face a choice between two different tax-bill impacts rather than one number, decided at May town meeting and on the ballot.
The lower tier's dollar figure now includes restoring fifth-grade band, and stormwater funding was pulled out of the override question entirely for now.
The boards themselves said the top tier is not guaranteed to be the last override ask, which residents should weigh alongside whatever figures appear in town-meeting materials.

ours.headline: TriBoard formally voted to pursue a two-tier (not single-number) FY27 override, dropping stormwater from it

watch_next: The tri-board override meeting the following night
The override vote at town meeting and the town election

what_happened.line: The committee voted to ask town meeting for only its lowest override tier, not a higher amount.
It voted to accept a reduced fallback budget for use if that override fails.

The fallback adds an English learner teacher, restored assistant principals, and a special education position, while cutting athletic trainer hours, sports, transportation, custodial and technology lines.
Middle school sports stay cut even if the override passes, to keep the requested amount manageable.
The committee voted to stop paying this year's Massachusetts Association of School Committees dues.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked to vote on this override at the tri-board meeting, town meeting and the town election; a no vote triggers the fallback cuts described above.
The fallback ties athletic and band transportation cuts to preserving staffing positions at the primary and Turkey Hill schools, a trade-off the committee named directly.
Class sizes and support staffing at the primary school depend on whether the assistant principal and special education positions are funded or cut.

ours.headline: School Committee locked in its override request; without it, elementary classes grow and sports/band busing are cut.

watch_next: Town meeting, May 2
Superintendent's team report on reallocating the athletic-transportation cut to restore a teacher and OT aide position

what_happened.line: The committee voted to send the Select Board one override number, built from a "core" budget option, instead of asking for two tiers.

It also voted to accept a no-override "balanced" budget but cut athletic transportation instead of a teacher, and told staff to find a way to restore that teacher and an occupational therapy aide position.
Members added back a small music-teacher position to the override budget to preserve fifth-grade band.
The committee voted to move forward on a richer health-insurance opt-out incentive for employees who decline coverage.
A resident in public comment asked, without answer in the minutes, what happened to money left over from a prior override.

why_it_matters: Town meeting voters will be asked to approve a single override figure built from this "core" budget, so this is the number that reaches the ballot.

If the override fails, whether a classroom teacher and an occupational therapy aide keep their positions now depends on how the district reallocates the athletic-transportation cut, a decision still pending from the superintendent's team.
The health-insurance opt-out change affects what the town and school pay employees who decline coverage, on both the town and school side of the budget.

ours.headline: Committee picked one override number (core "Scenario C") and, if it fails, will cut athletic transportation to save a teacher and a therapy aide

watch_next: School Committee meeting, March 18, 2026 — presentation of the balanced/cuts budget
A tri-board decision on override structure and amount, targeted for late March/early April 2026, ahead of the ballot-language deadline

what_happened.line: The three boards voted unanimously to place a Proposition 2½ override question on the ballot, with no final amount set that night.
A straw poll on a single combined override versus two tiered options came out closely split, with the count itself unclear in the recording and several members absent.
Rather than issue a joint statement on the straw poll, each board agreed to share updates through its own channels, since the Select Board had not yet finished its own line-by-line budget review.
The boards set a goal of agreeing on an override number by late March or early April, ahead of the deadline to hand ballot language to the town clerk.
The School Committee will present its balanced, cuts-based budget at its March 18 meeting.

why_it_matters: Whatever number the boards settle on becomes the property tax increase every household is asked to approve at town meeting.

A single override versus a tiered one changes what is guaranteed to residents versus what depends on a second vote later — school staff positions were named specifically as at stake in either version.
The March 18 School Committee presentation of the cuts budget is the baseline every override option is being measured against.

ours.headline: TriBoard split near evenly on one FY27 override vs. two tiers, but agreed unanimously to put one on the ballot.

watch_next: Legislative advocacy letter, aimed to be finalized and sent by March 18
A final decision on the FY27 athletic trainer/athletic director staffing structure, still tabled

what_happened.line: The superintendent told the committee a math error had overstated the FY27 budget deficit and gave a corrected, lower figure.
The committee tabled a decision on cutting the athletic trainer position for a cheaper EMT staffing model, with at least one member opposed to tabling.
The committee decided not to pursue outsourcing custodial and facilities staff and will not revisit it on the agenda.
The committee set a rough FY27 override target without restoring full athletic staffing, leaving that question open.
The superintendent's office agreed to begin producing a quarterly HR staffing report for the committee.

why_it_matters: The corrected deficit changes the size of the gap the FY27 override is meant to close, which affects what residents are eventually asked to fund.
The still-unresolved athletic trainer vs. EMT question affects coverage for student athletes and is tied to the override ask.
Custodial and facilities jobs stay in-house rather than being outsourced, the outcome raised repeatedly in public comment.

ours.headline: Superintendent corrected a budget math error, lowering the FY27 deficit; athletic trainer cuts left undecided

watch_next: March 18 School Committee meeting, where the specific cuts needed for a balanced (non-override) budget are to be discussed
Finance committee's review of the FY27 needs-based restoration budget the School Committee voted to send it

what_happened.line: The committee voted to send the finance committee an FY27 budget it says the town cannot fund without an override.
Members said they favor one unified, townwide override rather than separate amounts by school or grade.
The committee will not detail what gets cut to balance the budget without an override until its March 18 meeting.
The committee also approved several grant proposals, capped virtual-school enrollment, and adopted the FY26-27 school calendar.
A speaker during public comment urged the committee to hold off alarming the public until the actual funding need is known.

why_it_matters: This budget is described as restoring positions cut the prior year, and the committee says funding it depends on an override, a vote that would raise property taxes beyond the normal cap.
Residents will not see which specific programs or positions are at risk if the override does not pass until the cuts are laid out at a later meeting.
The grant, enrollment-cap and calendar votes are procedural and do not depend on the override outcome.

ours.headline: Committee advanced a "needs" FY27 budget it says the town cannot currently fund without an override

watch_next: The written budgeting handbook, to be produced once the current budget season concludes
The FY27 budget, to see whether grant-funded staff are fully removed from operating lines as described

what_happened.line: School officials called the FY25 surplus a budgeting failure rather than found money, tracing most of it to a competitive paraprofessional grant that freed already-budgeted funds nobody reallocated.
No votes were taken; the committee described new practices already adopted, including regular budget updates and pre-approval of grants.

Officials committed that in FY27 anyone paid through an entitlement grant will be fully moved off the operating budget line, and the district will stop budgeting a line it is also seeking a competitive grant to cover.
A stabilization account meant to cushion swings in out-of-district placement costs has been established but remains unfunded.
Residents pressed on withheld budget documents, transparency around grant-funded lines, MCAS reading scores, and whether another override will be needed.

why_it_matters: The surplus and the accounting changes bear on how the FY27 school budget is built, which sets what the town is asked to raise, not just what the district reports it needs.
The stabilization line for out-of-district placements sits behind a cost category that can move sharply and without warning when a child's placement changes.
A written budgeting handbook and any future override request will be the next points where residents can see whether these changes hold.

ours.headline: School officials call the FY25 surplus a budgeting failure, not lost money, and warn FY27 will be tight

watch_next: February 9th tri-board meeting at the middle-high school, where an override number and updated staffing data are expected
Updated school staffing figures, including last year's layoffs, to be supplied by the school committee

what_happened.line: Town, school and finance officials agreed Lunenburg likely needs a property-tax override to close a projected FY27 gap, without settling on an amount or structure
The Town Manager walked the boards from updated state aid down through health insurance, retirement, transportation and a fourth fire shift to a remaining deficit
Finance and school committee members disputed whether district staffing has actually been cut, and the school committee agreed to supply updated data including last year's layoffs
The boards agreed to seek the state's override-options guidance and campaign-finance rules before any public campaign, and set a joint follow-up for February 9th

why_it_matters: If the boards move forward, residents would eventually vote on an override, which raises the property tax bill outside the normal levy limit -- and the town's April 10th ballot deadline is setting the pace of these discussions.

The named cost drivers -- health insurance, the county retirement assessment, transportation, and a fourth fire shift -- were described as largely fixed, meaning any budget relief this year would have to come from elsewhere or from new revenue.

The unresolved dispute over whether school staffing has grown or been cut touches what positions and services the school budget can protect, and residents will be asked to weigh that when an override figure is presented.

ours.headline: Town, school and finance officials agree Lunenburg likely needs a property-tax override to close a large FY27 budget gap

watch_next: Turkey Hill Elementary directive vote, planned two meetings from this one
public budget forum date, to be set at the next School Committee meeting

what_happened.line: The business manager was directed to prepare a second FY27 budget with strategic-investment additions alongside a level-services option, as a flat town revenue scenario was called not viable.
The committee approved a Student Opportunity Grant reallocation toward decodable readers and math materials.
The committee approved a revised preschool tuition schedule adding a five-day option.
Turkey Hill Elementary capital planning discussion favored new construction over rehab within a proposed cap on the town's cost share, with a vote deferred to let an absent member weigh in.
A special education line item transfer was approved to cover rising ASL interpreter costs.

why_it_matters: Whether the town approves an override this year will decide which of the two FY27 school budgets goes forward, and that shapes any cuts or new spending residents are asked to fund.
Preschool families will see a new tuition schedule and a five-day enrollment option take effect.
The Turkey Hill decision, still unvoted, will set the direction and town cost share for a major school building project.

ours.headline: Committee plans two FY27 budgets, banking on a town override; without one, deep cuts loom

watch_next: Next tri-board meeting, January 27, in Town Hall
A public forum on the possible override, date to be scheduled

what_happened.line: Officials said that once health insurance costs are covered, the FY27 budget leaves almost no room for raises, cuts, or level services, pointing toward a tax override.
No vote was taken at this joint Select Board, Finance Committee, and School Committee session.
The audit line was underbudgeted for FY27, with costs expected to rise sharply as only two municipal auditors remain licensed in Massachusetts.
The Town Manager proposed a new, standalone assistant town manager position, to be funded for half of FY27.
The group agreed to hold a separate public forum on a possible override, though no date was set.

why_it_matters: A property tax override would go to voters and would raise bills beyond the state's normal levy cap, and officials here signaled they see it as likely for FY27.
Rising fixed costs -- health insurance, an audit line, IT/Munis software -- absorb new town revenue before it reaches raises, staffing, or school and town services.
A new assistant town manager position is a town-side staffing addition, separate from the school budget rule 11 governs.

ours.headline: Officials warn the FY27 budget leaves almost nothing after health insurance, pointing toward an override

watch_next: The next tri-board meeting, where the boards aim to settle on one override figure
A future school committee vote on Tony's rebuild-vs-new framework for Turkey Hill

what_happened.line: The committee voted to permanently return the Kids Kingdom playground to town control.
After an update on the track/turf field project, the committee agreed to ask the superintendent to request a placeholder warrant article for the engineering funding.
A member was tasked with drafting a framework for deciding between rebuilding Turkey Hill or building new under MSBA before that choice comes back for a vote.
The committee said it wants to align with the select board and finance committee on one override figure at the next tri-board meeting.
The business manager reported FY26 spending on track, running slightly ahead of the same point last year.

why_it_matters: Returning Kids Kingdom shifts upkeep and liability for that playground from the school district to the town.
A placeholder warrant article for the track/field project, and a coming decision on rebuilding versus replacing Turkey Hill, are steps toward items that could appear on a town ballot.
The push for one shared override number across the three boards signals that residents may be asked to vote on a single town-wide tax increase rather than separate asks.

ours.headline: School Committee votes to hand the Kids Kingdom playground back to the town for good.

watch_next: The School Committee's own vote on its FY27 budget, expected before the town manager issues her budget number
The finalized FY2025 budget variance statement, after edits are sent to Dr. Fortuna

what_happened.line: The committee said it cannot sustain further staffing cuts and would not choose between a full-time athletic director/trainer and reading interventionists in the FY27 budget.
Members plan to vote their own FY27 school budget before the town manager sets her budget number, a change in sequencing from past years.
Any override request would go to the May town meeting rather than a November special town meeting, because November needs a higher approval threshold.
The committee voted to finalize its FY2025 budget variance statement, pending edits sent to the superintendent that do not change its message.
Officials disclosed a paraprofessional staffing gap in the current FY26 budget that had gone unaccounted for, but said the year should still close out okay.

why_it_matters: The choice between a full-time athletic director and reading interventionists is left open, so families may not know until later in the FY27 process which program gets funded.

An override, if requested, would appear on the May town meeting warrant rather than a November special vote, and this cycle's cuts would be discussed in broad categories rather than naming specific positions.
A paraprofessional undercount already found in the FY26 budget is a data gap worth watching for whether it recurs or grows in the FY27 numbers that underlie any override ask.

ours.headline: Committee says it won't choose between a full-time athletic director and reading interventionists in FY27.

watch_next: December 17, 2025 budget workshop
April 2027 MSBA statement-of-intent submission for Turkey Hill

what_happened.line: Committee said the FY27 school budget likely needs an override, with further work at a December 17 budget workshop.
Committee approved a France/Switzerland trip after debate over cost and equity, though the vote outcome was not clearly audible on the recording.
A federal grants review flagged risk to Title I, Title II, Title IV and special-education funding, recommending conservative FY27 budgeting for those grants.
District will pursue a Massachusetts School Building Authority statement of intent for Turkey Hill targeting an April 2027 submission rather than a competitive application this year.
Two policies -- middle school pathway exploration and competency determination -- passed on third read.

why_it_matters: An override would ask residents to vote on raising taxes above the levy cap to close the FY27 school budget gap.
Federal grant risk to Title I/II/IV and special education could shift costs onto the town-funded school budget if those funds shrink.
The Turkey Hill building decision sets the timeline and state-funding path for any future renovation or construction, which affects future borrowing and tax bills.

ours.headline: Committee previews an FY27 school budget gap likely needing an override; also OK'd a costly France trip.

watch_next: The later public forum where deferred FY25 questions, including the negative-transfer explanation, will be addressed.
Next budget cycle's presentation, expected to include a grants/revolving-fund breakdown and roster-level health insurance detail.

what_happened.line: Three boards jointly previewed a forward-looking FY27-29 school budget outlook; no votes were taken on any item.

The district asked to restore several staff positions cut in FY26 -- interventionists, a kindergarten paraprofessional, world language and music teachers, an ELL teacher -- framed as restoration rather than expansion.
A full-time athletic director/assistant principal restoration was debated without resolution; administration was asked to bring back position history and a data-backed model.
The business manager will research the source of negative transfers shown in the FY25 budget summary, with FY25 questions otherwise deferred to a later public forum.
Presenters agreed to report health insurance cost increases separately from the total budget ask, and to provide roster-level health plan enrollment detail for the next budget cycle.

why_it_matters: These are preview requests for the FY27 budget residents will eventually vote on at town meeting; nothing here is a commitment or a final figure.

Health insurance and utility cost assumptions shown in this preview flow into the same budget-versus-override conversation that has confused residents in past cycles, which is why presenters agreed to break the insurance line out separately.

Whether the district can distinguish grant-funded and general-fund positions -- requested for the next cycle -- affects how residents should read any staffing line as a town cost versus a grant that could end.

ours.headline: District previews FY27-29 outlook, asking to restore staff cut in FY26; no vote was taken.

watch_next: Revised draft statement on the FY25 surplus, for possible release/approval at the next School Committee meeting
Decision on whether to submit an MSBA statement of interest for Turkey Hill Elementary this cycle

what_happened.line: The superintendent's preliminary FY27 budget memo restores paraprofessional, interventionist and other positions cut in recent years.
The committee voted to raise substitute teacher pay after finding Lunenburg paid the least of five neighboring districts.
The committee voted to approve a revised FY27 capital plan and continued weighing whether to seek state building assistance for Turkey Hill Elementary.
A proposed cashless athletics-campus payment policy was sent back to the policy subcommittee after resident feedback.
A member said the school budget's health insurance line makes its year-over-year increase look larger than other town departments'.

why_it_matters: The preliminary FY27 memo signals a shift from recent cuts and will move through the district's budget process toward a town meeting vote.
Raising substitute pay changes a line item residents will see in the FY27 budget and affects staffing coverage in classrooms.
How the health insurance line is presented can shape comparisons between the school budget's growth and the town's other departments.

ours.headline: Superintendent's preliminary FY27 budget restores paraprofessional and intervention positions cut in prior years.

watch_next: School Committee workshop on committee operating norms, Nov. 12 at 7pm
Second readings of the advertising, Monty Tech pathway, cashless payment, and competency determination policies

what_happened.line: The committee agreed to a staged, multi-meeting process for deciding whether to renovate or replace Turkey Hill Elementary, starting with building needs before cost or funding options.
Rather than have the facilities director attend the next meeting, the committee will first collect written feedback from Turkey Hill staff on what the building needs.

The committee took first readings on four policies -- advertising in schools, a Monty Tech pathway program, cashless payment at events, and competency determination -- and sent each to a second reading.

The Trust Fund Commission's chairman told the committee that school-related gifts and trusts are town property under statute and asked that scholarship and donor records be turned over to the treasurer's office for review.
The committee approved routine items: two line-item transfers, four donations, and a new scholarship named for James J. Larkin.

why_it_matters: The renovate-versus-rebuild choice for Turkey Hill will eventually come before residents as a building project and a tax question, and how much the state's MSBA program reimburses depends on which path the committee picks.

The four policies now headed to a second reading -- including cashless payment at school events -- will return for further debate before they take effect, and could change how families pay for or access school activities.
A request to catalog school-related trusts and scholarships touches funds set aside for student scholarships and could affect who has authority to approve them.

ours.headline: Committee begins staged process to decide whether to renovate or replace Turkey Hill Elementary, no vote yet

watch_next: Superintendent's first-year evaluation goals, a formal committee vote next meeting
FY28 budget town halls at each school, scheduled for mid-November

what_happened.line: The committee reversed a prior vote and released the already-purchased soccer uniforms to players this season.
It voted to accept a one-time state legislative earmark, putting part of it toward primary-school touch screens and restoring the I-Ready assessment tool.
An accountability report described concerning third-grade reading and special-education subgroup scores, tied in part to earlier budget cuts.
The superintendent presented her FY28 budget priorities and first-year evaluation goals, both set for a formal vote next month.
The committee accepted three PTO donations to the schools.

why_it_matters: The uniform reversal and one-time earmark spending do not set district policy, but the FY28 budget priorities laid out here will shape the budget request residents are eventually asked to fund.
The reading and special-education score concerns, and the earlier cuts they were linked to, bear on how much the district asks for in literacy and special-education funding next year.
Weak paraprofessional pay and looming union contract renewals were raised as pressures the FY28 budget will need to absorb.

ours.headline: Committee reversed itself, voting to let soccer teams wear the new uniforms already purchased

watch_next: November town meeting vote on the special reserve/stabilization fund warrant article
Policy subcommittee's proposed pre-approval policy for spending outside the certified budget

what_happened.line: The committee voted to place a special reserve fund for unbudgeted out-of-district special education and transportation costs on the November town meeting warrant.
A separate warrant article seeking additional Chapter 70 funding, an amount as heard, was withdrawn in favor of pursuing it through the regular FY27 budget process.
The committee approved two new paraprofessional positions and restoring a full-time IT support position, both drawn from the salary reserve line.
A proposal for an outside comprehensive audit of FY25 finances, funded from returned free cash, was deferred pending talks with the town manager.
Football and soccer uniforms bought without required purchase-order approval will not be penalized retroactively; undistributed soccer uniforms will be held for next year's replacement rotation.

why_it_matters: The reserve fund is a warrant article residents will vote on at November town meeting; it would let year-end school budget surplus automatically cover special education placement and transportation costs that come in over budget.
Withdrawing the Chapter 70 warrant article means any additional state aid this year would not be spent immediately but would instead be weighed against other priorities in the FY27 budget process.

The unauthorized uniform purchases and the salary-reserve-funded hires prompted the committee to signal it will develop a policy requiring pre-approval before staff spend outside the certified budget.

ours.headline: Committee backed a special-ed reserve-fund warrant article but withdrew a separate bid for extra Chapter 70 money

watch_next: Further FY27 budget presentations and any votes on the storm water utility fee or the fourth fire shift
DPW's outsourcing-vs-hiring cost spreadsheet, to be sent to the finance committee

what_happened.line: The Select Board, School Committee and Moderator unanimously appointed Stephanie Quinn to the Montachusett Regional Vocational School Committee.
The boards also authorized a three-year Council on Aging services agreement with the Montachusett Regional Transit Authority.
The regular Tri-Board session that followed was entirely FY27 preliminary budget presentations from DPW, Facilities, Fire and Police, with no votes taken.
DPW outlined a proposed storm water utility fee and was asked to send its full analysis comparing town crews to outsourced snow and ice work to the finance committee.
Fire presented a proposed fourth career shift, with when any new hires would actually start left to be worked out later with the town manager.

why_it_matters: The proposed storm water utility would be a new fee on residential and business properties, separate from the tax bill, and is still in the preliminary stage.
A fourth fire shift and DPW staffing and equipment requests shown here will feed into the FY27 budget residents eventually vote on at town meeting.
No budget figures were adopted or voted at this meeting -- these were department presentations, not decisions.

ours.headline: Boards unanimously appointed Stephanie Quinn to the Montachusett Regional Vocational School Committee.

watch_next: Revised FY27 capital plan priority list, due to the capital planning committee by October 1
Next School Committee meeting: deferred vote on the capital plan and the superintendent's goals

what_happened.line: The business manager reported a reconciled FY25 school budget surplus, attributed mainly to a paraprofessional line double-budgeted against a grant plus underspending on maintenance, custodial and instructional lines.
Officials said the surplus did not affect the separate cuts already made to the FY26 budget.
The committee replaced a generator with the turf field/track project on the draft FY27 capital plan priority list, to be sent to the capital planning committee by October 1.
The business office agreed to start monthly budget-to-actual reporting to the committee after residents said prior requests for such reports had gone unanswered.
The committee also passed routine items: four line-item transfers, a music-boosters donation, a state arts grant application, new legal counsel, and added secretarial hours at the high school.

why_it_matters: The surplus explanation and the new monthly budget-to-actual reports speak to how closely residents can track whether school spending matches what was voted, not to who was at fault for the earlier mismatch.

The turf field/track project's move onto the capital plan, financed through borrowing, is a future debt-service item that would show up in the town's capital budget and tax bills once financing is worked out.
The added secretarial hours and legal counsel change are funded from existing lines and do not appear to require new town money.

ours.headline: FY25 school budget surplus of roughly $600K traced largely to a grant line double-budgeted, unspent
