watch_next: Continued hearings for 10 Parmenter Road and New West Townsend Road on September 14th
Zoning bylaw cleanup items (section 2534, shared-driveway cap) at the November special town meeting

what_happened.line: Planning Board approved special permits for flood-plain reconstruction at 881 Flat Hill Road and 18 Oak Ridge Road, and a multi-dwelling rebuild at 27 Fire Road 15A.
Hearings for 10 Parmenter Road and New West Townsend Road were continued to September 14th after a board member's absence created a quorum risk.
The board also endorsed a lot-line land swap between two Page Street properties.

The board discussed requiring applicant materials by noon the Thursday before a meeting, and flagged zoning bylaw items -- including a possible removal of the multiple-dwelling approval provision and a four-dwelling cap on shared driveways -- for the November special town meeting.

why_it_matters: Three properties got special-permit approval with standard conditions, clearing the way for flood-plain reconstruction and a multi-dwelling rebuild to proceed.
Neighbors and applicants for the Parmenter Road and New West Townsend Road projects have their hearings pushed to September 14th rather than decided tonight.
A proposed submission-deadline policy and zoning bylaw changes headed toward the November special town meeting could change how future permit applications are handled and what residents vote on.

ours.headline: Planning Board approved flood-plain and multi-dwelling special permits for three properties; two hearings continued for lack of quorum.

watch_next: Town counsel's input on the inclusionary bylaw draft, expected before the 24th
A fall public forum on the draft bylaws, before the May 2027 town meeting warrant

what_happened.line: Planning Board reviewed second drafts of cluster, senior, and inclusionary zoning bylaws aimed at the May 2027 town meeting, taking no substantive votes.
The board asked for payment-in-lieu percentages to be recalculated by development-size tier for the next draft of the inclusionary bylaw.
A bylaw change affecting dwelling-unit counts on common driveways was tabled until the state legislature acts on a possible statewide duplex-by-right mandate.
The board asked the building inspector for an opinion on whether the existing inclusionary bylaw applies to the Parmiter Road development.
The board set a plan to brief other town boards individually and hold a fall public forum, favoring the library or senior center over the high school as venue.

why_it_matters: These zoning bylaws, if placed on the warrant, would go to voters at the May 2027 annual town meeting and could change what developers must pay or build for affordable units.
The payment-in-lieu percentage under revision affects how much money the town collects from housing developments in place of built affordable units.
Whether the inclusionary bylaw is found to apply to the Parmiter Road development could determine affordable-unit requirements for a project already in progress.

ours.headline: Planning Board revised draft zoning bylaws for cluster, senior, and inclusionary housing for the 2027 town meeting

watch_next: August 24, 2026 Planning Board meeting: continued hearings on 10 Parmentor Road and 860 New West Townsend Road, plus a vote on disbanding the master plan steering committee
August 10, 2026 working session on revised zoning bylaw drafts

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to accept and approve the town's master plan after roughly five years of work.
The board approved a site-plan modification at 475 Lemonster Shirley Road adding manufacturing as a permitted use alongside warehouse distribution.
Hearings for 10 Parmentor Road and 860 New West Townsend Road were continued to August 24 because the board lacked a quorum able to vote.

The board leaned toward forming its own master plan implementation committee rather than asking the Select Board to do it, and plans to vote on disbanding the old steering committee at the next meeting.

why_it_matters: Adopting the master plan sets the framework the town will use for zoning bylaws and land-use decisions brought to future town meetings.
The site-plan approval allows manufacturing use, alongside existing warehouse distribution, at that Lemonster Shirley Road property.
Residents following the Parmentor Road or New West Townsend Road proposals, or the fate of the master plan steering committee, should watch the August 24 meeting.

ours.headline: Planning Board formally adopted the town's master plan after a roughly five-year process

watch_next: Next Planning Board working session, August 10
Eventual bylaw language brought to town meeting

what_happened.line: The board raised the cluster-housing density cap for single-family units from two to four per acre.
It restored a payment-in-lieu option and an offsite-unit option for developers triggering inclusionary housing, ramping with unit count.
A draft requirement for full site plan review on minor changes near residential abutters was dropped in favor of the existing, more easily amended regulations.
Letters of credit were removed as an allowed performance guarantee for cluster developments, leaving cash, a AAA-rated bond, or a covenant.
The board left out an under-18 occupancy restriction from the draft senior housing bylaw so it can still carry inclusionary housing requirements.

why_it_matters: These are working drafts of zoning bylaws headed toward town meeting, and the density, buffer, and guarantee choices made here will set the terms any cluster or senior housing project has to meet.
The inclusionary housing provisions determine whether new development contributes cash or units toward affordable housing, and how much.

ours.headline: Planning Board drafted zoning changes for minor site plan review, cluster housing, and senior/affordable housing.

watch_next: July 27, 2026 Planning Board meeting: continued votes on the Parmenter/Round Road and 860 New Westminster Road permits, and a vote on the master plan update
Town counsel's review of the draft HOA for 860 New Westminster Road, expected by July 27

what_happened.line: The board continued two multi-lot subdivisions, Parmenter/Round Road and 860 New Westminster Road, to July 27 for more engineering and maintenance review.
Residents raised concerns about storm-water runoff toward Lake Shirley, driveway placement, and a possible wildlife corridor on Parmenter Road.
The board approved three smaller items: a duplex conversion on Reservoir Road, a driveway and storm-water change on Arbor Street, and a storm-water permit on Mass Ave.
A vote on the draft master plan update was pushed back two weeks so members can finish reviewing it individually.

why_it_matters: Homeowners near Parmenter/Round Road and New Westminster Road will see construction timing hinge on a maintenance mechanism (HOA or covenant) and a fire-system cistern review still being worked out.
Runoff and possible wildlife-corridor questions raised by neighbors could affect lot layout and tree clearing before those subdivisions get final approval.
The board is also weighing changes to its common-driveway and inclusionary-housing bylaws over the summer, which could affect how future subdivisions and duplex conversions are permitted.

ours.headline: Board delayed two large subdivisions over storm-water/wildlife concerns; approved several smaller projects

watch_next: July 13 continuation hearings for 10 Parmenter Road, New West Townsend Road, and 934 Mass Ave
July 20 zoning-bylaw editing session, a posted and filmed public meeting

what_happened.line: The board closed hearings and approved all permits for a self-storage facility at 30 Summer Street, with added construction-hour limits.
The board also closed the hearing on 1325 Mass Ave and approved the office building's site plan and a related stormwater change.
Two subdivisions, at 10 Parmenter Road and New West Townsend Road, were continued to July 13 pending engineering and fire-protection review.
The board accepted a bond for remaining work at 189 Electric Ave and directed enforcement against a neighboring unpermitted driveway.
The board approved decommissioning-bond language for a solar battery storage project and heard a report on ADA-compliance costs at Turkey Hill School.

why_it_matters: Two commercial projects -- a self-storage facility and an office building -- cleared their local permitting, moving them toward construction with conditions on hours and site work.
Residents near 10 Parmenter Road and New West Townsend Road will see further town review of drainage, driveway construction and fire access before those subdivisions can proceed.
A committee report flagged that bringing Turkey Hill School into ADA compliance is difficult and costly, a signal of a possible future capital request.

ours.headline: Board approved permits for a 30 Summer St. storage facility and a 1325 Mass Ave. office building

watch_next: June 22 Planning Board meeting: continued hearings for 934 Massachusetts Avenue, 30 Summer Street, 10 Parmentor Road, and 860 New West Townsend Road
Summer working sessions on new housing and site-plan zoning bylaw language, ahead of a future town meeting vote

what_happened.line: Board members opened the meeting saying the failed override is a mandate to expand commercial zoning for revenue, before any bylaw language exists.
Board approved the Subaru dealership redevelopment at 757 Chase Road, adding conditions on vehicle loading and pre-installation soil testing.
Board found a proposed change at 171 Arbor Street not a minor (de minimis) modification and sent the storm water question to outside peer review, billed to the applicant.
Board kept its slate of officers and committee appointees unchanged for the year and continued three other pending site applications to June 22.

why_it_matters: The board's stated reading of the override result could shape future proposals to rezone land for commercial use, which would affect where new business development is allowed in town.
The Chase Road approval and the Arbor Street peer-review referral affect what conditions nearby residents can expect on drainage, traffic and site work for those specific projects.
Three pending applications (30 Summer Street, 10 Parmentor Road, 860 New West Townsend Road) and the Unitil substation storm water hearing move to June 22, when residents can next weigh in.

ours.headline: Board says the failed override is a mandate to expand commercial zoning for revenue

watch_next: June 8, 2026 Planning Board meeting: 10 Parmenter Road, 860 New West Townsend Road, and 30 Summer Street are all continued to that date.

what_happened.line: The board continued the nine-lot 10 Parmenter Road/Ruth Street stormwater and common-driveway application to June 8, pending peer review and fire-department sign-off on access.
The board closed hearings and approved stormwater and site-plan permits for 222 West Townsend Road, 60 Crossroad, and a motor-vehicle sales site at 149 Summer Street, each with standard conditions.
The board recommended the select board auction the Hollis Hill Road tax-title properties, including the former Lake Lodge, rather than have the town fund redevelopment.
A lakefront resident asked that flooding concerns from clear-cutting at the 10 Parmenter Road site be passed to the project's review engineer before it returns.

why_it_matters: The 10 Parmenter Road continuance affects a nine-lot subdivision's stormwater and driveway plans, with a neighbor's flooding concerns still to be addressed before any vote to approve.
Recommending auction of the Hollis Hill Road parcels would move two town-held properties toward private sale instead of municipal use, unless another board steps forward with funding first.
The approved permits at three sites clear conditions for construction to proceed there this year.

ours.headline: Planning Board approved several site/stormwater permits and continued the 10 Parmenter Road subdivision pending review.

watch_next: May 11, 2026 Planning Board meeting: vote on the Hollis Road tax-title properties and continued storm water permit hearings (60 Cross Road, 222 West Townsend Road, 860 New West Townsend Road)

what_happened.line: The board could not vote on whether the town should keep two tax-foreclosed Hollis Road properties, pushing the decision to May 11.
Storm water permit hearings for two other developments were continued to May 11 pending further review.
The board approved a storm water permit for the Zero Reservoir Road development after adding a requirement for town counsel to review the HOA document.
After residents raised concerns about erosion and incomplete hydroseeding, the board set a cash bond for stabilization work at 7-Eleven Mass Ave, not releasable before November 1, 2026.

The chair noted a change in state tax title law now requires the town to pay a foreclosed owner the difference between what was owed and the property's appraised value, rather than keeping the full property.

why_it_matters: Whether the town keeps or disposes of the Hollis Road properties affects options like municipal or senior housing use, and the new tax title law changes what the town owes a former owner either way.
Residents near the 60 Cross Road and 222 West Townsend Road sites raised drainage and erosion concerns that remain unresolved until the May 11 hearing.
The bond set at 7-Eleven Mass Ave is meant to ensure erosion and hydroseeding work gets finished, with the money held until vegetation is established.

ours.headline: Board can't vote yet on whether the town should keep two tax-foreclosed Hollis Road properties.

watch_next: 27 April, 6:35 p.m. — continued hearings on storm water permits for 222 West Townsend Road and Zero Reservoir Road
Draft easement/deed language for Zero Reservoir Road's shared drainage system, due to town counsel before the next meeting

what_happened.line: The board directed the applicant at Zero Reservoir Road to draft easement or deed language for a shared drainage system, for town counsel to review.
The board accepted a bond, in the amount as heard, so 181 Electric Avenue can get its occupancy permit, holding release until year-end.
The board voted to tell the select board it does not want to pursue the town's right of first refusal on 35 Lemonster Road.
Storm water permit hearings for new house lots at 222 West Townsend Road and Zero Reservoir Road were continued to 27 April after abutters raised well and runoff concerns.
The board adopted a revised, simplified fee schedule for storm water and plan-review permits after comparing fees to surrounding towns.

why_it_matters: Who maintains a subdivision's shared drainage system determines who pays if it fails later, a question that follows the property rather than the builder.
The bond lets an occupancy permit issue now while tying its release to stabilization work checked over two growing seasons, not verified immediately.
Declining the right of first refusal is a vote that forgoes the town's option to buy 35 Lemonster Road, relevant to residents tracking open space and land purchases.

ours.headline: Board weighed shared-drainage liability on two subdivisions and approved a bond so 181 Electric Ave can get its occupancy permit

watch_next: Revised Planning Board fee schedule expected at the first April meeting
Formal adoption of the reorganized standard storm water permit conditions, not yet voted

what_happened.line: Board endorsed the ANR subdivision plan for 10 Parmentor Road after confirming Round Road as a public way.
Board approved a new vehicle maintenance building at 39 Intervail Road, the Amazon distribution site, with standard conditions.
Board granted a two-year extension of the 494 Electric site plan permit.
Board informally agreed the Parmentor Road applicant can phase storm water permits by lot group instead of bonding all unbuilt lots at once.
Board discussed reorganizing its standard storm water permit conditions to add inspection lists and recorded drainage easements.

why_it_matters: The storm water phasing arrangement changes how construction guarantees work on a large subdivision, which matters to neighbors who raised drainage concerns about the new driveways.
The Intervail Road approval lets construction proceed on the Amazon site's vehicle maintenance building under specified conditions and hours.
A townwide revision to standard storm water conditions, if adopted, would apply to future site plan permits beyond this meeting.

ours.headline: Board endorsed the 10 Parmentor Road ANR subdivision and approved a vehicle maintenance building on Intervail Road.

watch_next: Continued hearings for the townhome project and other applications, 13 April 2026
Zoning amendments proposed for the next annual town meeting

what_happened.line: The board settled on four zoning amendments to bring to the next annual town meeting: inclusionary zoning, senior housing, minor site plan review, and cluster development.
The 20-unit townhome project on New West Townsend Road was continued to mid-April pending fire department review of the driveway and engineering review.
The board advised the select board to decline the town's first right of refusal on Chapter land at Northfield Road.
De minimis site plan changes were approved for a rooftop solar/battery project and for a garage rebuild.

why_it_matters: The zoning amendments, if brought to town meeting, would change rules for housing density, senior housing, and small-project review townwide.
The continued hearing means the townhome project's fire-access and engineering questions are unresolved and will return for another public hearing.
Declining the right of first refusal clears the way for the Northfield Road land to be sold or developed privately rather than held or acquired by the town.

ours.headline: Planning Board sets its FY27 zoning-amendment priorities and continues two housing hearings pending fire/engineering review

watch_next: February 23, 2026 meeting: Zero Reservoir Road and 30 Summer Street hearings resume
Written feedback on the draft master plan due ahead of the February 23 meeting

what_happened.line: The Zero Reservoir Road common driveway and storm water hearings were continued after a lot was found to lack frontage on the correct street.
The board approved a scenic road alteration and stone wall and tree removal at 1083 Northfield Road, with conditions.
The board approved Walmart's site plan for restriping its parking lot and relocating pickup parking at 301 Mass Ave.
The board endorsed a revised ANR plan and found related driveway and storm water changes de minimis at 1083 Northfield Road.
Fewer than a quorum of the board will attend a joint Select Board storm water task force meeting to avoid an open meeting law problem.

why_it_matters: The frontage problem at Zero Reservoir Road means that project's driveway and storm water permits are on hold until the next hearing.
Property line and driveway changes at 1083 Northfield Road and the Walmart lot changes at 301 Mass Ave are now approved, affecting nearby traffic and site conditions.
Contamination at the former 925 Mass Ave gas station site was raised in public comment and is now tied to a working group the board just appointed a member to.

ours.headline: Board approved Walmart parking changes and Northfield Rd tree/wall removal; stalled Reservoir Rd project over a frontage rule.

watch_next: January 26, 2026 Planning Board meeting -- continued votes on 30 Summer Street, Zero Reservoir Road, and 1083 Northfield Road
Revised 10 Parmentor Road ANR, due within six months for the fee waiver to apply

what_happened.line: Board voted 4-0 to deny endorsement of the 10 Parmentor Road subdivision plan, finding Fire Road 15 lacks adequate width, grade and construction, but agreed to waive refiling fees if a revised plan comes back within six months.
Board granted a one-year extension of the construction start deadline for the 485 Leominster Shirley Road battery storage project, citing tariff-related delays outside the applicant's control.
Three other matters -- a storm water permit for 30 Summer Street, a storm water permit for Zero Reservoir Road, and a scenic road permit for 1083 Northfield Road -- were each continued to January 26.
Capital Planning Committee submitted its project rankings but said how much money will actually be available for this year's capital budget is still unclear.

why_it_matters: The 10 Parmentor Road denial means any subdivision relying on Fire Road 15 frontage cannot proceed until the road issue is resolved, though the fee waiver lowers the cost of trying again.
Residents tied to the 30 Summer Street, Zero Reservoir Road and 1083 Northfield Road applications will not get a decision until the January 26 meeting.
An unclear capital budget outlook affects which municipal projects the town can fund this year, pending the town's broader finance and staffing picture.

ours.headline: Board declined to endorse a 35-lot Parmentor Road ANR over Fire Road 15's inadequacy, waiving refiling fees

watch_next: Continued storm water permit hearing for 0 Reservoir Road, January 5 at 6:05pm
Capital Planning Committee's capital budget figure, once reported

what_happened.line: The board announced a new planning and economic development director had been hired as the three-year master plan process concluded.
A public hearing on a storm water permit for a proposed 4-lot subdivision on Reservoir Road was continued to January 5 amid board concern over a shared driveway's safety near a road curve.
The board set, then accepted, a bond as a performance guarantee for a completed home on Townsend Harbor Road, contingent on the check clearing before occupancy.
The Capital Planning Committee reported it does not yet have a capital budget figure this year, expecting it later than usual due to finance department turnover.
The board endorsed an Approval Not Required plan for a West Townsend Road property.

why_it_matters: The Reservoir Road subdivision review continues into January, with the shared driveway's winter safety still unresolved before four new house lots can move forward.
A capital budget figure arriving later than usual this year may compress the town's review window once it is finally available.
The bond and ANR actions are routine land-use approvals that do not change anything residents will be asked to vote on.

ours.headline: Town hires a new planning/economic development director as the three-year master plan process wraps up.

watch_next: December 15 Planning Board meeting: continued 30 Summer Street hearing
Graves' peer review findings on 30 Summer Street site plan and stormwater permit

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to send the proposed multi-story self-storage project at 30 Summer Street out for peer engineering review.
The board then continued the 30 Summer Street public hearing to December 15.
Members questioned the applicant on parking counts, truck turning movements, and flood-plain stormwater compliance without resolving those questions.
A performance bond for a stormwater permit at 100/116 Towns Harbor Road was tabled until the applicant supplies a planting cost estimate.
Judy Dragos was appointed to the open seat on the Economic Development Committee.

why_it_matters: The 30 Summer Street self-storage hearing stays open through peer review, so its site plan, parking and stormwater design can still change before the board votes on approval.
The stormwater permit bond at Towns Harbor Road cannot be set, and won't be, until a cost estimate arrives -- delaying that permit.
Neither vote grants or denies a permit; both keep the applications in process for the December 15 meeting.

ours.headline: Planning Board opened hearings and sent a proposed multi-story self-storage project at 30 Summer Street to peer review.

watch_next: Open Space Committee's draft bylaw, modeled on Medway's, going to the bylaw review committee before returning to the Planning Board for a vote.
Confirmation from the Agricultural Commission and town counsel before the Planning Board formally votes to add that seat.

what_happened.line: Board approved a special permit for a ground-mounted solar array at 560 Mulpus Road, conditioned on Board of Health septic sign-off and interconnection paperwork.
Board also approved a stormwater permit for a Sunny Hill Road property, adding inspection conditions covering tree removal, erosion control, and the rain garden.
No members of the public spoke on either hearing.
Open Space Committee raised adding an Agricultural Commission seat and moving toward becoming an independent, bylaw-based committee; no vote taken yet.

why_it_matters: The solar permit sets conditions a developer must still clear before construction can proceed, and the board keeps a hook to revisit panel layout if septic requirements change it.
The stormwater permit's added inspection conditions are the mechanism the town uses to check drainage work actually gets built as designed.

A bylaw making the Open Space Committee independent, and adding an Agricultural Commission seat, would change who sits on it and how it is appointed — a governance change residents may see come back for a vote.

ours.headline: Board approved a special permit for a ground-mounted solar array at 560 Mulpus Road, plus a stormwater permit.

watch_next: November 10, 2025: continued public hearing on the 255 Sunny Hill Road storm water permit
Town meeting vote on the MBTA Communities bylaw and the common driveways amendment

what_happened.line: The board closed hearings and voted to recommend an MBTA Communities compliance bylaw that meets the state mandate by raising the density cap at the existing Tritown development rather than rezoning new land.

A contested storm water permit for 255 Sunny Hill Road was continued to November 10 after abutters raised unresolved drainage-pipe and past lawsuit concerns and outstanding taxes on the property came up.
The board also voted to recommend removing the paving requirement from the common driveways bylaw.
The chair changed practice so open, non-agenda public comment is discouraged going forward; residents are asked to email the planning office to get items placed on the agenda.

why_it_matters: The MBTA Communities recommendation goes to town meeting as a zoning bylaw vote, and choosing a density increase at Tritown over new sites is the mechanism the town is proposing to meet the state mandate.

The Sunny Hill Road continuance means the drainage dispute, the lawsuit concern between the applicant and an abutter, and the property's tax status remain open before any storm water permit is issued.
The change to public comment practice affects how residents get an item onto a Planning Board agenda going forward.

ours.headline: Board votes to recommend MBTA Communities compliance via a density bump at Tritown, not new sites

watch_next: October 2 warrant submission deadline for MBTA Communities zoning language
October 27 public hearing on MBTA Communities zoning

what_happened.line: The board closed the hearing and approved, with conditions, a special permit and site plan for a home ground-mount solar array at 390 Goodrich Street.
Conditions include posting a decommissioning bond before occupancy, sized to the array's removal cost, plus documentation of wiring and the utility interconnection agreement.
Board members said the town's solar bylaw is outdated and raised hiring a planner to update it.
The board agreed that MBTA Communities zoning language from its consultants should go on the town meeting warrant, ahead of an October 2 submission deadline.
The board put off responding to the Master Plan Steering Committee's request for feedback on the town's master plan.

why_it_matters: This sets the bonding and documentation conditions a homeowner installing a ground-mount solar array in Lunenburg can expect to meet.
The solar bylaw is described as outdated, so residents proposing solar projects may see zoning terms change before their own applications are heard.
MBTA Communities zoning language is headed for a town meeting warrant article, meaning residents will be asked to vote on it.

ours.headline: Planning Board approved a special permit and site plan for a home ground-mount solar array on Goodrich Street, with conditions.

watch_next: Public hearing on the MBTA Communities zoning bylaw, October 27
Warrant article language deadline, October 2

what_happened.line: Planning Board approved both permits for a 5-lot common driveway at 1083 Northfield Road, over one member's objection that it functions as an unpermitted subdivision.
The board denied the applicant's request to waive the bylaw's paving-material requirement and will consider a warrant article to remove that requirement instead.
The public hearing on the draft MBTA Communities zoning bylaw amendment was pushed from September 22 to October 27, with warrant article language due October 2.
The board recommended the Select Board waive the town's first right of refusal on the West Townsend Road open space parcel and endorsed an ANR plan at 830 Massachusetts Avenue.
Members raised extensive concerns that the Master Plan Steering Committee's draft recommendations are too vague to act on.

why_it_matters: The Northfield Road approval sets a precedent for using the common-driveway process to divide land the way a subdivision would, which affects how future multi-lot developments in town can proceed.
The MBTA Communities zoning bylaw determines how the town complies with the state's multi-family housing law, and residents will get a vote on it at Town Meeting after the October 27 hearing.
The warrant article on common-driveway paving requirements and the West Townsend Road open space decision both go before Town Meeting and the Select Board respectively.

ours.headline: Planning Board approved the Northfield Road common driveway permit despite a member's subdivision-precedent concerns.

watch_next: September 22 Planning Board meeting: public hearing on MBTA Communities zoning
September 8 Planning Board meeting: continued review of the 830 Massachusetts Ave ANR application

what_happened.line: The board approved a site plan for an addition to the Pat Brody cat shelter at 499 Northfield Road, conditioned on a stormwater maintenance plan.
The chair set a goal of holding a public hearing on MBTA Communities zoning compliance on September 22, contingent on the consultant finishing bylaw language in time.
The board extended review of a lot-line application at 830 Massachusetts Ave to September 8 to clarify a dimensional question rather than denying it outright.
The board closed an incorrectly opened performance guarantee account for 430 Mulpus Road and had the town treasurer open a properly formatted replacement.
The chair warned applicants about fraudulent invoices being sent out on town letterhead.

why_it_matters: MBTA Communities zoning compliance sets what housing the town's bylaw must allow, and the September 22 hearing is the next public chance to weigh in before any change reaches town meeting.
The cat shelter approval and the Mulpus Road account correction are routine permitting and finance actions that keep an active local project and a town-held fund properly documented.
Anyone doing business with the town who receives an invoice on town letterhead should confirm it directly with the town before paying.

ours.headline: Board approved a cat shelter's expansion and set a Sept. 22 hearing on MBTA Communities zoning

watch_next: The released March 24 executive session minutes, once posted
Planning Board meetings scheduled for August 25 and September 8 at town hall

what_happened.line: Planning Board voted unanimously to release its March 24 executive session minutes without redaction.
The board found no error or sensitive content requiring further executive session before releasing them.
Board members agreed that any future error found in released executive-session minutes would be handled by voting to re-enter executive session, not raised publicly.
The meeting was virtual-only, drew no public attendance or comment, and lasted about seven minutes.

why_it_matters: This makes a previously closed-door Planning Board discussion from March 24 part of the public record, which residents can now request or review.
The vote itself sets no budget, policy or project outcome -- it only governs disclosure of past closed-session discussion.

ours.headline: Planning Board voted to release its March 24 executive session minutes to the public.

watch_next: Continued Northfield Road hearing at the August 25, 2025 Planning Board meeting
Stormwater task force's ERU-based fund proposal, expected at an upcoming town meeting

what_happened.line: The board closed the hearing and approved a scaled-down warehouse site plan and stormwater permit for 260 Fula Road, subject to conditions including a clean peer-review letter.
The Northfield Road hearing on a common driveway and stormwater permit was continued to August 25 amid concern the board lacked a full quorum able to vote.
The board voted to close an outdated stormwater guarantee account for 430 Mulpus Road and move the funds into a new one, with paperwork pending figures from the building inspector.
A town stormwater task force described a proposed fund that would charge every property, including commercial and institutional, based on its impervious surface area.
The board set a process to sign the outstanding West Townsend Road decision by email review and in-person signature rather than at a formal meeting.

why_it_matters: The Fula Road decision clears a warehouse project, reduced from its original size, to proceed with peer-reviewed stormwater conditions attached.
The Northfield Road continuance affects a pending common-driveway and stormwater permit; neighbors of that project wait until at least August 25 for a vote.
The stormwater task force's fund idea, if it reaches town meeting, would be a new charge tied to a property's paved and roofed area, applying to homes and businesses alike.

ours.headline: Planning Board approved a scaled-down 260 Fula Road warehouse; continued Northfield Road driveway hearing to August.

watch_next: July 28 Planning Board meeting: the two continued hearings, the signed decision document, and the MRPC seat assignment

what_happened.line: Public hearings for 1083 Northfield Road and 260 Fula Road were continued to July 28 because the applicants were not present.
A signed decision document for a previously approved project could not be located in the meeting packet and was short of signatures, pushing it to the next meeting.
The chair asked another board member to cover the MRPC seat for three meetings from September to December due to a scheduling conflict; no one was assigned.
Review of abutting-community notices in the packet was put off until a meeting when the full board is present.

why_it_matters: Anyone with a stake in the 1083 Northfield Road common driveway/stormwater permit or the 260 Fula Road site plan modification will need to watch for the July 28 hearing date instead.
A delay in signing the decision document means a previously approved project is not yet finalized on paper.
The board's MRPC representation and its handling of abutting-community notices remain open items that affect how neighboring towns' projects get reviewed here.

ours.headline: Planning Board continued two hearings and a decision to July 28 after applicants and paperwork weren't ready

watch_next: Continued public hearing on 260 Fuller Road, July 14, 2025
Draft MBTA Communities Act bylaw from the board's consultant, Community Scale

what_happened.line: Board voted 3-0 to direct its consultant to draft an MBTA Communities Act bylaw for the Tritown/Young's Road site, the paper-compliance option.
The 260 Fuller Road warehouse site-plan hearing, over contamination and drainage at a former dump site, was continued to July 14 after a peer-review fee was assessed.
Board voted 3-0 to close the hearing and approve the stormwater permit for 100 Townsend Harbor Road with standard conditions.
Matthew Brunner was re-elected chair 3-1 after a first vote for Matthew Allison failed 1-3.
Board voted to lower the Master Plan Steering Committee's quorum to five members.

why_it_matters: The MBTA Communities Act vote sets which zoning path the town will pursue for multi-family housing near transit, ahead of a bylaw the town will eventually vote on.
The Fuller Road contamination and drainage questions bear on a warehouse project's approval and on water quality flowing toward Hickory Hills Lake.
A lower quorum makes it easier for the Master Plan Steering Committee to hold meetings and act going forward.

ours.headline: Board voted to direct its consultant to draft an MBTA Communities Act bylaw for the Tritown/Young's Road site.

watch_next: November special town meeting vote on the single bylaw option the planning board selects
Written resident feedback submitted on note cards at this meeting

what_happened.line: Planning board will bring exactly one MBTA Communities zoning option to a November special town meeting, per its consultant agreement.
No vote was taken; this was a public input session, and the chair and many residents leaned toward 'paper compliance' using Tritown's existing zoning.
That approach would reserve Leominster Shirley Road for a separately, locally designed mixed-use development rather than for MBTA compliance.
Residents pressed unresolved questions about school enrollment, water and sewer capacity, and who any new housing would actually serve.

why_it_matters: This shapes the single zoning bylaw residents will be asked to vote on at the November special town meeting, and which sites see new housing capacity.
A 'paper compliance' approach would meet the state mandate largely on paper, without necessarily adding housing units, according to several residents at the meeting.
Water, sewer and school-capacity questions raised here were not answered in this session and remain open going into that vote.

ours.headline: Planning Board leans toward Tritown 'paper compliance' to meet the state's MBTA Communities housing mandate

watch_next: June 23, 2025 Planning Board meeting: chair re-vote and continued hearing on the 100 Townsend Harbor Road stormwater permit
July 14, 2025: continued hearing on the 1083 Northfield Road five-lot plan

what_happened.line: The Planning Board's chair election tied twice between Matt Allison and Matt Brener and was left unresolved, to be revisited June 23.
The board and the Open Space Committee both voted to recommend the town not exercise its right of first refusal on land at 222 West Townsend Road.
A special permit for a common driveway at 443 West Townsend Road lot 3 was approved with three bylaw waivers.
A stormwater permit hearing for 100 Townsend Harbor Road was continued to June 23 after abutters raised concerns about runoff into Hickory Hills Lake.
A hearing on a revised five-lot plan at 1083 Northfield Road was continued about a month pending peer review.

why_it_matters: The tied chair vote leaves the board without a settled leader going into its next meeting, though vice chair, clerk, and committee-representative seats were filled without contest.
Declining the town's right of first refusal on the West Townsend Road parcel means it can be sold and developed rather than held for conservation, adding it to the tax rolls instead.
Residents near Hickory Hills Lake get another chance to weigh in on stormwater runoff from the Townsend Harbor Road project before the board rules on the permit.

ours.headline: Planning Board chair election tied between Allison and Brener; unresolved, revisit June 23

watch_next: June 9, 2025 continued hearing on the Towns and Harbor Road storm water permit and the 1083 Northfield Road permits
Scheduled public information sessions on MBTA Communities zoning options

what_happened.line: Board leaned toward minimal 'paper compliance' rezoning, using the already-built Tritown complex to meet the state's MBTA housing mandate rather than adding new capacity elsewhere.
The board voted to require a peer-review deposit and continued the Towns and Harbor Road subdivision's storm water hearing to June 9.
The chair will schedule public information sessions on MBTA Communities zoning options, to be posted under the Open Meeting Law.
A scenic-road tree removal at 63 Lancaster Avenue was approved after the hearing closed.
The board added a Finance Committee member to the Master Plan Steering Committee.

why_it_matters: The MBTA Communities compliance choice determines whether new zoning capacity for housing is concentrated at one already-built site or spread to new land elsewhere in town.
The storm water peer review, funded by an applicant deposit, addresses residents' flooding and groundwater concerns near the proposed five-lot subdivision.
Planned public information sessions on MBTA Communities zoning are residents' chance to weigh in before any rezoning vote.

ours.headline: Planning Board leans toward minimal 'paper compliance' rezoning of Tritown to meet the state's MBTA housing mandate

watch_next: Annual town meeting vote on the ADU and floodplain warrant articles
May 12 Planning Board meeting — MBTA Communities contractor presentation

what_happened.line: Board voted to recommend town meeting approve the state-mandated ADU zoning bylaw, which drops the owner-occupancy requirement.
Board voted to recommend town meeting approve an update to the floodplain and flood insurance rate map bylaw.
The public hearing on both bylaws closed with no residents attending or commenting.
Board voted to enforce the peer-review deposit already written into its rules and regulations rather than adopt a new fee procedure.
Board approved a de minimis site-plan change at 110 Pleasant Street for a foundation extension.

why_it_matters: Town meeting will be asked to vote on the ADU bylaw, which changes what accessory dwelling units can be built without an owner living on site.

The floodplain bylaw update ties to FEMA flood maps; residents in affected areas will get handout instructions at town meeting to check their own property against the federal tool rather than individual notice.
The peer-review fee decision keeps an existing an amount as heard deposit requirement in place for applicants going through board review, rather than creating a new pre-payment procedure.

ours.headline: Board recommends town meeting approve ADU zoning change that drops the owner-occupancy requirement

watch_next: Consultant (Community Scale) presentation of MBTA Communities compliance options, May 12
Board's compliance-option decision, due by late June, preceded by public information sessions

what_happened.line: The Planning Board must choose an MBTA Communities zoning compliance option by late June, after a consultant presents options and the board holds additional public information sessions.

The Municipal Building Design Committee reaffirmed a majority recommendation to demolish the Brooks House and will use its existing cost estimate as the town meeting warrant article ask, without a separate vote on that figure.
The board endorsed an ANR plan creating two lots at 60 Cross Road.
The chair is covering extra hours at the planning office while the land use director is unavailable.

why_it_matters: The MBTA Communities decision sets the zoning option the town will live with under the state law, and the public sessions before June are residents' chance to weigh in before it is locked in.
The Brooks House demolition recommendation and its warrant article will come before town meeting as a dollar ask, using a cost estimate that was not re-voted on by the committee.
The ANR endorsement for 60 Cross Road allows that property to be split into two buildable lots without further Planning Board review.

ours.headline: Board must pick an MBTA Communities zoning compliance option by late June, after public input sessions

page.overview:
If you choose to use the drop box located at the Lancaster Avenue entrance of the Ritter Building, please notify the Planning Board office.
The Planning Board consists of five members elected for terms of five years each. The Planning Board shall make careful studies of the resources, possibilities, and needs of the town and shall make plans for the development of the town. The Board shall make a comprehensive or master plan, setting forth in graphic and textual form policies to govern the future growth and development of the entire town. The Board shall have the power to regulate the subdivision of land within the town by the adoption of rules and regulations governing such development and the administration of such rules and regulations. The Planning Board shall make recommendations to the town meeting on all matters affecting land use and development, including the zoning by-laws of the town.
Zoning Bylaws are for sale at $35 per copy and the Rules and Regulations Governing the Subdivision of Land are for sale at $90 per copy. Both can be accessed on this page and are also available for purchase at the Planning Office, Ritter Memorial Building, 960 Massachusetts Avenue.

what_happened.line: PACC voted to prepare a warrant article seeking more money at the November special town meeting to cover an anticipated FY27 shortfall.
The manager said the FY27 salary line is tight because he took his vacation time as a payout this year instead of spreading it over three years.
The committee reprioritized its FY27 goals, moving a studio and storage space solution to the top of the list.
A cable licensing/advisory committee update covered legal counsel and survey work ahead of an eventual Comcast contract renegotiation.
The committee set its next meeting for October 5.

why_it_matters: A warrant article at the November special town meeting means residents will be asked to approve additional funds for the cable access budget.
A tight FY27 salary line tied to a one-time vacation payout is a budget mechanism worth watching as the committee finalizes its funding request.
Ongoing work toward a Comcast contract renegotiation, and the legal cap on the franchise fee, will shape how public access programming is funded going forward.

ours.headline: PACC will seek a November special town meeting warrant for more money as FY27 salaries run tight

watch_next: July 6th, 6 p.m., Wallace Room: PACC's organizational meeting to fill two open seats and set the year's calendar
The new cable advisory committee's first meeting, to be scheduled after June 16th

what_happened.line: The failed town override, not the base FY2027 budget, is why town concerts have no funding this year.
The same override failure is eliminating a town staff position that handled website updates, social media and IT liaison work.
A PACC member will take over doing the committee's own website updates once that town position is gone.
The committee set July 6th at 6 p.m., in the Wallace Room, as an organizational meeting to fill two open PACC seats.
A new cable advisory committee's membership was agreed, pending select board appointment, with its first meeting to be scheduled after June 16th.

why_it_matters: Losing the town concerts and a town website/social-media/IT position are direct, ongoing effects of the override vote failing, separate from the base budget that did pass at town meeting.
Committee volunteers, not town staff, will now maintain the town website work this position used to do, a shift in who is responsible for that service.
Two open seats on this committee will be filled July 6th, a door for a resident who wants to serve.

ours.headline: Failed town override cuts town concert funding and a town staff position, pushing website work onto PACC volunteers

watch_next: Volunteer names for the Comcast license renegotiation committee, targeted for June
Next PACC meeting, June 1st at 6 PM

what_happened.line: PACC began recruiting residents for a separate committee to renegotiate the town's Comcast cable license before it expires.
The FY27 budget approved at Town Meeting draws on retained earnings to cover cable operations, pending state requalification of those funds.
The committee corrected its draft minutes to note an investment figure was an estimate set by the town treasurer, not one the committee determined.
The committee plans to meet before the end of June to reconcile its investment/trust fund figures with the finance department's own posting.

why_it_matters: The Comcast license renegotiation will shape the terms and revenue that fund the town's cable and public-access operations for years to come.
The FY27 cable budget's use of retained earnings is not yet finalized, since the state must first requalify those funds.
The committee's own investment figures currently do not match the town's official financial report, which affects confidence in the numbers reported to the public.

ours.headline: PACC began recruiting a citizen committee to renegotiate the town's Comcast cable license.

watch_next: Town meeting warrant articles for the FY27 PEG budget shortfall and the Castis system replacement
Next PACC meeting: the tabled policy vote and the enterprise fund investment status report

what_happened.line: Both the FY27 public-access budget shortfall and an aging broadcast-system replacement will go to town meeting as warrant articles, partly funded from retained earnings, without a committee vote.
A shortfall in this year's salary line was covered by shifting money out of the equipment, advertising, and maintenance lines rather than a new appropriation.
The committee decided to keep optional add-ons, including a mobile app and a branded streaming channel, in the broadcast-system quote for now and reassess after a year.
A vote on committee policy was tabled because a required member was absent.
A discrepancy in the health-insurance cost estimate for next year's budget was left unresolved, with the manager assigned to follow up.

why_it_matters: Town meeting will be asked to approve warrant articles drawing on the cable fund's retained earnings for both an operating shortfall and new equipment.
Covering this year's salary line by moving money out of equipment and advertising shows the budget already running tight before the fiscal year closes.
A new ADA-mandated audio description requirement and an unsettled health-insurance figure could add to what the FY27 budget needs to cover.

ours.headline: PACC will ask town meeting to tap retained earnings to close a budget gap and replace its aging broadcast system.

watch_next: FinCom presentation of the FY27 budget, targeted for March 5
Formal vote to remove the obsolete videographer-editor job title, expected at the next PACC meeting

what_happened.line: PACC voted to approve its amended FY27 budget presentation, which shows a shortfall covered by retained earnings, for delivery to FinCom.
The committee authorized its manager to present that budget to FinCom, after lowering its Comcast franchise-fee revenue projection to a more conservative basis.
A new legal-fees line was added to the FY27 budget ahead of upcoming Comcast franchise contract negotiations.
PACC voted to appoint two of its members to a newly approved town Cable Advisory Committee that will eventually handle Comcast franchise renewal.
The committee continued early-stage, unresolved talks about sharing studio space with FATV in Fitchburg, with another meeting set for March 4.

why_it_matters: The FY27 cable budget, funded mainly by Comcast subscriber fees rather than property taxes, still goes to FinCom for review as part of the town's overall budget process.

A new legal-fees line and the incoming Cable Advisory Committee mark the start of the town's renegotiation of its Comcast franchise agreement, which sets what residents pay and what services the cable channel gets.
A shortfall covered from retained earnings means the committee is drawing down savings rather than raising fees this year, a choice that has a limit if adopted repeatedly.

ours.headline: PACC approved its FY27 budget for FinCom, showing a shortfall to be covered from retained earnings

watch_next: A member will draft and circulate an email requesting a meeting with the town manager on the warrant process
FY27 budget update expected next month, ahead of a Tri-Board meeting

what_happened.line: The committee found the annual town-meeting warrant had been changed before town meeting to add an unexplained sum, without anyone telling them.
A special-meeting warrant article meant to fix that also carried a small videographer pay increase, and the whole article was pulled before town meeting.
Rather than vote on the matter, the committee chose to send one or two members to meet informally with the town manager about the warrant process.
The station manager reported the salaries line is tracking toward a shortfall six months into FY26, with a firmer figure due in February.
A town committee is weighing moving the cable studio into the Ritter building's second floor.

why_it_matters: This is a dispute over whether a town committee's budget line can be changed on a warrant without notice to that committee -- a process question that could affect how any board's warrant article gets amended.

ours.headline: PACC to seek a meeting with the town manager after being shut out of two warrant changes

watch_next: The FY27 budget proposal's review by the Tri-Board
A PACC policy book, to be compiled and posted to the PACC website

what_happened.line: PACC voted unanimously to send its FY27 budget proposal, showing expenses outpacing income, to the Tri-Board.
The gap between projected revenue and expenses is planned to be covered from the committee's retained earnings rather than new funding.
The committee removed references to specific legislative funding-split percentages from the Tri-Board presentation because those ratios are not yet confirmed.
PACC voted unanimously to approve its bylaws as amended for a channel-number correction.
The committee has not received notice of Cable Advisory Committee meetings despite being told a seat was arranged, and will email the town manager to ask.

why_it_matters: The FY27 budget PACC is sending to the Tri-Board draws on the committee's own reserves rather than requesting more from the town, so it does not directly affect the tax rate.
A Cablecast server replacement and outside legal counsel for the Comcast franchise contract are the named drivers of expenses exceeding income in that budget.
The bylaws vote and the budget proposal now move to the Tri-Board process, where a resident could follow how the shortfall is handled.

ours.headline: PACC reviewed its FY27 budget, showing a projected shortfall to be covered from retained earnings

watch_next: Next PACC meeting, November 3rd
Resolution of the warrant/line-item repayment with the town's finance office

what_happened.line: The committee is planning a costly server replacement at the start of FY27, calling the current unit end of life after nine years.
The town's finance office flagged confusion over a warrant the committee submitted, tied to a budget-line repayment not yet assigned to a specific line.
Studio relocation continues, with cameras still needing wiring and no dedicated storage room secured.
A new videographer was already in place before the prior one resigned, so the position did not go vacant.
The committee set its next meeting for November 3rd and will take up normalizing and posting its policies then.

why_it_matters: A major equipment purchase planned for FY27 will show up in the committee's budget request and its enterprise fund balance.

An unresolved repayment tied to a prior annual town meeting appropriation is a loose end between the committee and the town's finance office that residents may see resurface in a warrant or budget line.
The unfinished studio move affects when and where public meetings and programs, including town meeting coverage, can be recorded.

ours.headline: PACC covers the studio move, a costly new Castis server purchase, and a warrant repayment mix-up with the town.

watch_next: Next regular PACC meeting, October 6
Secretary's compiled master-plan feedback document, once circulated to the committee

what_happened.line: PACC decided to place its studio-space and building-use needs under the master plan's municipal-buildings goal, not only the community-gathering-spaces goal.
The secretary was assigned to compile every member's edits into one final feedback document; members were told to send comments only to the chair, per open meeting law.
The committee agreed to flag potential costs -- videographer and staff time, a studio build-out -- as a budget concern in its written response, without settling on a figure.
PACC cited its own governing town-bylaw sections as the basis for its answers under both master-plan goals.
No members of the public attended this special session.

why_it_matters: This shapes what space and infrastructure requests the town's master plan will carry forward for the cable committee, which can influence future capital or budget requests for a studio build-out.
The committee flagged staffing and build-out costs as concerns without a figure, so any dollar amount will need to come later through the normal budget process, not this planning input.
The bylaw citations tie PACC's requests to its existing legal mandate, which is the basis it would point to if it later asks the town for space or funding.

ours.headline: PACC drafted its written input to the town's master plan, adding studio-space and building-use goals

watch_next: Special town meeting vote on the warrant article transferring PEG enterprise fund retained earnings
Added PACC meeting, tentatively the following Monday, to finish the Master Plan Steering Committee questionnaire

what_happened.line: PACC voted to combine a repayment for FY26 items that could not be encumbered earlier with added videographer costs into one special town meeting warrant article.
That article would transfer money out of the PEG cable enterprise fund's retained earnings.
The station manager's first-pass FY27 budget showed expenses, driven mainly by salaries, rising against flat revenue, projecting a shortfall.
A member asked the manager to price replacing the aging Casters recording system for FY27 and check if it could also support an added HD channel.
The committee could not finish a Master Plan Steering Committee questionnaire and set an added meeting limited to that item.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked at a special town meeting to approve a transfer from the cable enterprise fund's retained earnings, drawing down a reserve rather than raising taxes.
A projected FY27 shortfall, driven largely by salaries against flat revenue, could mean a larger draw on that same reserve or other funding in next year's cable budget.
A possible capital request to replace aging recording equipment could surface in FY27 capital planning.

ours.headline: PACC voted to ask the special town meeting to transfer over $35,000 from the enterprise fund to cover a shortfall

watch_next: Next PACC meeting: September 9, 2026, 6 p.m.
S2556's progress through the Senate Ways and Means Committee

what_happened.line: The move into the renovated PAC studio is delayed at least two more weeks while the room is painted and floors sealed.
The manager will pursue filling two videographer openings, pending confirmation with HR.
Committee meetings will default to 6 p.m. going forward, falling back to 3 p.m. only if 6 p.m. is unavailable.
A state Senate bill that would tax streaming services to help offset falling cable franchise fee revenue has passed committee and moves next to Senate Ways and Means.
The next PACC meeting was set for September 9th at 6 p.m.

why_it_matters: The studio timeline affects when public access programming resumes from the renovated space residents may visit or appear on.
The streaming-tax bill (S2556) is a proposed new funding source for public access stations as cable franchise fees decline with cord-cutting -- it has not yet passed the full Senate.
The committee flagged FY27 budget items -- specialized legal/OPEB advice and the cable contract renewal ahead of its February 2028 expiration -- that will surface in a future town budget.

ours.headline: PAC's new studio move stays delayed at least two weeks as painting and wiring work continue.

watch_next: Next PACC meeting, August 4th at 3:00pm

what_happened.line: The committee authorized a replacement video-storage system (NAS) after the old one failed entirely, funded from the maintenance line for an amount as heard on the recording.
The committee reorganized for the new fiscal year, appointing a chair, vice chair and clerk/secretary, though those votes are not audible in the recording.
The committee will start recording trust fund commission meetings and, from the next day, tri-board meetings of the select board, school committee and finance committee.
Studio relocation to the TCP/TC Pasios space is planned for mid-to-late July.
The next meeting was set for August 4th at 3:00pm as a schedule exception.

why_it_matters: Failure of the video-storage system put the archive of recorded public meetings at risk; the committee treated the fix as routine maintenance spending rather than a capital purchase, so it did not require a separate town vote.
Adding trust fund commission and tri-board meetings to the recording schedule would give residents video access to bodies not previously covered.
The Comcast cable contract, the studio move and FY27 budget prep were all discussed but not resolved, so residents following public access should expect more decisions on those at future meetings.

ours.headline: Committee authorized a replacement video-storage system after the old one failed entirely

watch_next: Select board interviews of the two prospective committee applicants
FY27 budget and annual report materials, now expected to begin in July

what_happened.line: The cable studio must relocate into a single shared classroom once the building wing housing it closes, expected after August 1.
The committee asked the town manager to inform the select board that a member will serve as its liaison on the Comcast contract.
Annual report and FY27 budget preparation will start in July instead of the usual February, at the town manager's request.
July and August meeting times were moved to the afternoon to accommodate members' schedules.
The Comcast payment for the quarter was noted as lower than the prior quarter, though it had not yet posted to the trial balance.

why_it_matters: A forced move of the public-access studio into shared classroom space could affect where and how local programming, including school and town meeting coverage, gets produced going forward.

Starting FY27 budget work in July rather than February gives the town manager, capital planning and the finance committee more lead time on this committee's request, which residents may see reflected in an earlier budget calendar.
No votes with financial consequence were taken; the reported figures on the Comcast payment are as heard on tape and unconfirmed against the trial balance.

ours.headline: PACC's studio must move into one shared classroom as its building wing is closed by August.

watch_next: Next PACC meeting: facilities director's response on possible relocation sites for the studio
Comcast franchise contract renewal process, once a committee volunteer is identified

what_happened.line: The town plans to demolish the back of the Pacios building, which houses the PACC studio, with no relocation site confirmed.
Voters at town meeting rejected the new town hall and Marshall Park articles, removing options the committee had been counting on for a future studio.
The manager will informally ask the facilities director about relocation plans and report back at the next meeting; no motion was put to a vote.
The committee treated an FY26 budget line concern about indirect costs as resolved because it passed through town meeting's consent calendar.
The committee's investment fund, built to help offset the cost of a future studio, will instead be drawn on to cover operating costs as Comcast franchise fee revenue declines.

why_it_matters: Residents who rely on public access cable programming and municipal meeting broadcasts have no assurance the studio will have a home once the Pacios building's back end comes down.
The committee's reserve fund, once meant to help pay for a new studio, is now being described as a source to cover ordinary operating costs instead -- a change in what that money is for.
The FY26 budget line questioned by the committee already went through town meeting on the consent calendar, so no further town vote is expected on that point.

ours.headline: PACC has no confirmed new studio space as the town prepares to demolish its Pacios building.

watch_next: The warrant article as it appears on the town meeting warrant, and the vote on it
June, for whether the town moderator agrees to host the revamped Talk of the Town

what_happened.line: The committee reworded its town-meeting warrant article with the town manager to address resident concern that no tax money fund cable access.
It approved its March 3rd minutes without discussion.
Pre-production on a new knitting show is on indefinite hold at the host's request.
Talk of the Town is being redesigned as a segmented show, with the town moderator asked to host instead of the town manager to avoid a conflict of interest.
A presentation on new studio space went to the select board, and the committee said it does not yet know where that funding would come from.

why_it_matters: The warrant article's wording is what residents will read and vote on at town meeting, and it turns on whether cable access draws on tax dollars or a separate fee.
Studio space funding remains unresolved, so any cost would need to surface at town meeting before residents are asked to approve it.

ours.headline: PACC carefully reworded its town-meeting warrant article amid concern no tax money should fund cable access.
